full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party Nos. 1, 2, 5, 14, 301-317 and 239 to show cause as to why the Impugned Order No. 307 dated 16-4-1988 and Order No. 298 dated 9-11-1988 passed by the Assistant Judge, 1st Court, Patiya Upazilla, Chittagong in Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1988 (Partition Suit No. 103 of 1964) should not be set aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.

2. Facts relevant for disposal of the Rule, in brief, are that the predecessor of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1 and 2, Manikjan as plaintiff instituted Partition Suit No. 103 of 1964 in the First Court of Munsif, Patiya against the defendant-petitioner and opposite party Nos. 3-300 for a decree of partition of the schedule 1-18 to the plaint claiming saham of 1.71 acres of land. The defendant-petitioner No. 1 and his mother Masuda Khatun contested the suit by filing joint written statement. The trial court after contested hearing decreed the suit in preliminary form by judgment and decree dated 21-12-1976 determining the share of the contesting parties including the petitioner and his mother Masuda Khatun by issue Nos. 6 and 7 wherein the trial court specifically mentioned that the predecessor of the plaintiff-petitioner, Rahim Box was entitled to get Saham of 3.83 acres of land in the schedule to the plaint. After passing of the preliminary decree one Mr. Jalal Ahmed learned Advocate was appointed Commissioner for holding local investigation of the suit property and for allotment of share by metes and bounds maintaining respective possession of the parties. The learned Advocate Commissioner submitted a perfunctory, biased and baseless report giving the land in occupation of the petitioner to the share of the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1-2.

3. The trial court on the basis of Advocate Commissioner's report made the preliminary decree final on 14-7-1978. Against the final decree the petitioner and his mother Masuda Khatun (now dead) preferred Partition Appeal No. 32 of 1979 before the District Judge, Chittagong who upon hearing allowed the appeal and sent back the matter on remand to the trial court by setting aside the final decree by its judgment and decree dated 7-6-1986 for holding fresh local investigation in accordance with preliminary decree.

4. After remand, the petitioner filed an application on 5-8-1986 before the trial court praying for allotment of separate saham of 4.05 acres of land out of the schedule 1-18 to the plaint in his favour on payment of requisite court fee. The trial court allowed the application by his Order No. 283 dated 24-8-1986 and pursuant to the said order the petitioner deposited commission fee on 3-9-1986. On an application filed by the plaintiff-opposite party Nos. 1-2 the trial court by its Order No. 298 dated 9-11-1987 vacated the Order No. 283 dated 24-8-1986. Thereafter, the petitioner filed another application for recalling the Order No. 298 dated 9-11-1987 but the court rejected the same by its Order No. 302 dated 9-11-1988. The petitioner filed an application under Order 47 Rule 1 of the Code of Civil procedure for review of Order No. 298 dated 9-11-1987 which was registered as Miscellaneous Case No. 5 of 1988 and filed another application for appointment of Advocate Commissioner for the purpose of effecting partition. The said miscellaneous case along with the application for appointment of Advocate Commissioner was heard by the trial court and after hearing by its Order No. 307 dated 16-4-1988 rejected the same. At this stage, the petitioner moved this Court by filing this application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule and order of stay.

5. Mr. AKM Nurul Alam, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submits that the petitioner as defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing a written statement and the trial court while decreeing the suit more specifically in its judgment observed and found that the petitioner as heir of Rahim Box is entitled to get saham of 3.83 acres of land from schedule 1-18 to the plaint. He further submits that a partition suit in which preliminary decree has been passed is still pending. In a pending suit any party can seek saham whose share has been determined in the judgment, on payment of court fees. Accordingly, the petitioner filed an application praying for separate saham which was rightly allowed by the trial court by its Order No. 283 dated 24-8-1986 but by a subsequent order dated 9-11-1987 on an application of the plaintiff vacated the said order most illegally causing serious injustice to the petitioner and, as such, the court below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning failure of justice. The petitioner by an application urged upon the court to recall the order dated 9-11-1987 but in vain. Thereafter, the petitioner filed the Miscellaneous Case praying review of the said order but the trial court without assigning any reason most illegally rejected the same by order No. 307 dated 16-4-1988.

6. Heard the Learned Advocate for the petitioners, gone through the application, Impugned Order along with other annexures annexed thereto.

7. At the very outset to appreciate the submissions made by the petitioners counsel the Impugned Order may be looked into which runs thus;

“গত ধার্য্য তারিখ সরকারী ছৃটি থাকায় নথি অদ্য শুনানীর জন্য  পেশ করা গেল। পক্ষদ্বয় হাজিরা দিয়াছে। প্রার্থীকের দেওয়া মিচ দরখাস্তদয় শুনানীর জন্য লওয়া হইল। শুনলাম। দরখাস্ত না মঞ্জুর করা গেল।”

<u>8. From perusal of the impugned order passed by the trial court rejecting the review miscellaneous case, it appears that the court below has failed to give any reason in rejecting the miscellaneous case as to why the application is liable to be rejected. It is unfortunate to mention that the trial court in passing the impugned order is found to be unmindful and extremely calloused. The trial court ought to have understood that the litigants come before the court with a hope to get justice. In the present case, predecessor of the petitioners who contested the suit as defendant, filed an application praying saham of his share already determined by the preliminary decree. Passing of preliminary decree in a partition suit does not mean that the proceeding of the suit has been terminated finally unless a final decree is drawn. Therefore, after passing preliminary decree in a suit for partition, the parties to the suit can file application seeking separate saham so far determined by the court in the preliminary decree. In the instant case the trial court determined the share of the petitioner in its judgment observing that the petitioner is entitled to get saham of 3.83 acres of land. In this situation, it is not understandable why the petitioner will not get saham of the same on payment of requisites court fees in accordance with the law. It is now well known that in a suit for partition status of the plaintiff as well as the defendants are same and, as such, any party to the proceeding in a partition suit can apply for allotment of separate saham in their favour before drawing up final decree. Therefore, the trial court at the first instance rightly allowed the application by Order No. 283 dated 24-8-1986 but by a subsequent Order No. 298 dated 9-11-1987, unfortunately vacated the earlier order as such, committed a serious error of law. The petitioner though prayed for separate saham for 4.05 acres of land the trial court ought to have given saham at least 3.83 acres of land as determined and decided by the trial court. Since 0.22 acres of land as claimed by the petitioner is beyond the preliminary decree there is no scope to give saham of the said quantum of land to the petitioner.</u>

<u>9. Partition Suit in which preliminary decree has been passed is still pending and after passing the preliminary decree the defendant can apply seeking separate saham on payment of court fees required under the law. The trial court in not giving separate saham to the petitioners has committed an error of law in the decision occasioning failure of justice.</u>

10. Taking into consideration the above, this Court finds merit in the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner as well as in the Rule issued.

11. In the result, the Rule is made absolute, however, there will be no order as to costs. The impugned Order No. 307 dated 16-4-1988 and Order No. 298 dated 9-11-1987 passed by the Munsif, Patiya Upazilla (now Assistant Judge), 1st court, Chittagong are set aside and the Order No. 283 dated 24-8-1986 is restored. The trial court is directed to allot separate saham to the defendant No. 1 petitioners for 3.83 acres of land as determined by the preliminary decree.

12. Since the suit is of the year 1964 considering the antiquity of the suit the trial court is directed to dispose of the same within shortest possible time preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receipt of this judgment.

13. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule stands vacated.

Communicate a copy of this judgment to the Court concerned.

End.

full_judgment:
The instant Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and decree dated 14-5-1982 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No. 172 of 1980 affirming those dated 11-01-1980 passed by the learned Munsif, 2nd Court, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 840 of 1977, should not be set-aside.

2. The material facts relevant for disposal of this Rule, in short, is that the petitioners as plaintiff's instituted Title Suit No. 840 of 1977 in the Court of the learned Munsif, 2nd Court, Bagerhat against the defendants for Specific Performance of Contract and cancellation of the judgment and decree dated 7-9-77 passed by the same Court in Title Suit No. 665 of 1976 on the allegations, inter alia, that he sold the suit property to the defendants by a Kabala deed dated 12-9-1962 with an agreement to recovery of the same whereby defendant No.1 gave him an option to repurchase the suit land, if the price money be paid, within 10 years i.e. from 1369 BS to 1378 BS. The plaintiff's filed a Miscellaneous Case being No. P-3579 of 1973 in the Court of the then SDO and obtained an order of redemption and possession of the suit land. Then the defendant as plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 665 of 1976 for a decree of permanent injunction and for declaration that the order of redemption dated 11-6-1973 passed by the then SDO is null and void. The said Title Suit No. 665 of 1976 was decreed on contest by judgment and decree dated 07-09-1976. Hence, the plaintiff-petitioner has been compelled to file Title Suit No. 840 of 1977.

3. The opposite party as defendant No.1 contested the suit by filing written-statement stating, inter alia, that defendant No. I contested in the earlier suit by filing written-statements contending that he purchased the suit land from the plaintiff by a registered Kabala deed dated 12-9-1962 with an agreement to reconvey whereby he gave the plaintiff an option to repurchase the suit land, if the plaintiff is repaid the purchase money within 10 years, i.e. from 1369 BS to 1378 BS. The plaintiff obtained an ex-parte order of redemption and possession from the office of the Sub-Divisional Officer in Miscellaneous Case No. P-3579 of 1973 under PO 88 and PO 136 of 1972. Hence, he was compelled to file Title Suit No.665 of 1976 against the plaintiff for permanent injunction and for declaration that the order of redemption is void as the notice of the Miscellaneous Case was not served upon the plaintiff and suppressed the same with ill motive to obtain the ex-parte order. The plaintiff's suit was barred by Law of Limitation and prayed for dismissal of the suit. The learned Munsif dismissed the suit on the findings that "the case is not maintainable as the transaction was past and closed. Therefore, the suit was barred by the principles of waiver and estoppel. Moreso, the transfer which had already become absolute can not be affected and Hon'able High Court by a judgment declared the Section 95 (A) of SA&T Act as amended and PO 24, 88 and PO 136 of 1972 is discriminatory and unconstitutional."

4. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree passed by the Munsif, 2nd Court, Bagerhat dated 11-01-1980 in Title Suit No. 840 of 1977 the plaintiff as appellant preferred Title Appeal No. 172 of 1980 before the learned District Judge, Khulna. Eventually, the Title Appeal was transferred to the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna for hearing and disposal. The learned Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna, dismissed the appeal on 14-5-1982 on the findings that the plaintiff is not entitled to get a declaration that the decree dated 07-9-1977 passed in Title Suit No.665 of 1976 is void. Hence, confirmed the judgment and decree of the trial Court.

5. Being aggrieved by the judgment and decree dated 7-9-1977 passed by the Court of appeal below the petitioner preferred the instant revisional application before this Court and obtained the present Rule.

6. Mr Bivash Chandra Biswas, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submitted that both the Courts below in passing the judgment and decree committed error of law because the plaintiff-petitioner filed the suit after promulgation of PO 88 of 1972 claiming his relief under the law, but both the Courts below upon misconception of law took the wrong view and opined that the filing of the suit was barred by law of limitation as the date of agreement for reconvey expired in the year 1972 and the instant suit was filed after expiry of the period of limitation. He, by referring the pleading contained in the plaint submitted that it has been categorically mentioned therein

“অতঃপর বাংলাদেশ সরকার ১৯৭২ সালে পি,ও, ৮৮/১৩৬ নং আদেশ জারী করিলে এই বাদীপক্ষ উক্ত বিধান মোতাবেক গত ইং ১১-৬-১৯৭৩ তারিখ নালিশী জমি স্থানীয় এস,ডি,ও বাহাদুরের আদালত হইতে খালাশ করিয়া লয়েন এবং নালিশা ভুমি ১৯৭৩ সাল হইতে উক্ত আদেশ মোতাবেক দখল করিতে থাকেন। কিন্তু বিবাদী অত্রাদালতে দেঃ ৬৬৫/৭৬ নং মোকদ্দমা করিয়া এই বাদীর বিরুদ্ধে নিষেধাজ্ঞার আদেশ গত ইং ৭-৯-১৯৭৭ তারিখ প্রাপ্ত হইয়া নালিশী ভুমি বিবাদীপক্ষ দখল করিতেছেন বটে।(He, by) referring the decision to the case of Bangladesh vs Haji Abdul Gani Biswas, reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233 submitted that since the judgment passed by the High Court Division declaring the President's Order No. 88 and 136 of 1972 are unconstitutional as reported in 26 DLR 394, have already been reversed and allowed the Civil Appeal by the Apex Court declaring PO 24, 88 and 136 of 1972, 1973 are all valid laws for effecting necessary amendment in the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. Therefore, the judgment and decree passed by trial Court in Title Suit No.665 of 1976 and affirming the same in appeal was Coram non-judice and without jurisdiction. As both the Courts below, misread the relevant facts and law applicable in the case, as such, committed an error of law. He further submitted that the Appellate Division settled the legal proposition and principles regarding PO Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 by setting-aside and reversing the judgment of the High Court Division, for which it is imperative upon all concerned to uphold, preserve and persuade the judgment of Appellate Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court, therefore, institution of civil proceeding and obtaining decree by the opposite party respondent plaintiff in Title Suit No.665 of 1976 touching the merit of the order passed by the SDO in a proceeding arisen under Sections 95 and 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act 1951, which is the outcome of the legal consequences of the PO Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 is null and void as the Court was incompatible in passing the aforesaid judgment and decree.

7. At the midst of delivery of the judgment, Mr Shaik Razzaque Ali, the learned Advocate, who earlier appeared for the opposite party, informed the Court that the opposite party has taken back the brief from him, and, as such, he is not in a position to contest the Rule.

8. I have gone through the judgment of the Courts below and considered the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioner.

9. It appears that the plaintiff before filing the instant suit, on 12-09-1962 mortgaged the suit schedule property to the defendant with condition to repurchase the property within 10 years. Thereafter, on 3-08-1972 i.e. within 10 years of agreement President's Order No.88 was promulgated then the plaintiff filed an application before the then SDO for redemption of the property as per PO 88. and 136 of 1972, which was numbered as Miscellaneous Case No. P-3579 of 1973 and eventually the Miscellaneous Case was allowed by the SDO passing the order of redemption and directing the opposite party to hand over possession of the property to him.

10. The defendant without seeking any relief as per prevailing law, instituted a suit being Title suit No.665 of 1976 in the Court of Munsif, 2nd Court, Bagerhat and obtained a decree for permanent injunction and declaration that the order of redemption and possession handed over by the SDO in pursuance of PO Nos. 88 and 136 of 1972 is null and void, which was decreed.

11. Plaintiff, later, filed the instant suit being Title Suit No.840 of 1977 in the Court of Munsif, 2nd Court, Bagerhat for declaration and specific performance of contract challenging the judgment and decree dated 7-09-77 passed by the same Court in Title Suit No. 665 of 1976.

12. For convenience of discussions of legal issues and merit of the case, firstly, I would like to refer the prayers of the Title Suit No. 840 of 1977, which run as follows:—

“প্রার্থনাঃ

(ক) নালিশী ভুমি বাবদ বাদীর অনুকুলে বিবাদীর বিরুদ্ধে চুক্তি প্রবলের ডিক্রি ও দখল দিবার আদেশ হয়।

(খ) দেঃ ৬৬৫/৭৬ নং মোকদ্দমার ৭-৯-৭৭ তারিখের রায় বাতিলের ঘোষনা আদেশ হয়।

(গ) মোকদ্দমার যাবতীয় খরচার ডিক্রি হয়।

(ঘ) মূল বিবাদী পক্ষ আদালতের নির্দেশ মধ্যে আপোষ বাদীর বরাবর রেজিষ্ট্রি কবলা করিয়া না দিলে বাদীর নিকট হইতে খরচা গ্রহণে আদালত হইতে কবলা রেজিষ্ট্রি করিয়া দিবার আদেশ হয়।

(X) Equity, natural justice and pleadings দৃষ্টে বাদী তার যে কোন প্রতিকার পান তাহার ও আদেশ হয়।”

13. From the prayers "kha" and "Uma" of the plaint, it appears that the plaintiff prayed for declaration that the judgment and decree passed in Title Suit No. 665 of 1976 dated 7-9-1977 is void and be cancelled and also for further relief in equity and natural justice and in view of the pleadings of the suit sought for direction to restore possession of the suit property.

14. The Court below dismissed the suit with observation that the suit is barred by law of limitation, by referring the principles enunciated to the case of Hazi Abdul Gani Biswas, the precedent reported in 26 DLR 394 without considering the prayer "kha" and "Uma" of the plaint with the given facts of the case, as if, the suit was filed in pursuance of agreement dated 12-9-62. It is crystal clear from the pleadings that the plaintiff earlier initiated another case as petitioner by invoking the jurisdiction of the then SDO under PO 88 and 136 of 1972 read with Sections 95 and 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act and by an order dated 11-06-1973 obtained possession of the suit property in pursuance to a redemption order, which was challenged by the defendant in the Suit No. 665 of 1976.

15. The Court of appeal below while dismissing the appeal opined that the prayer portion of the suit shows that the plaintiff prayed for declaration that the decree passed in TS No. 665 of 1976 is void but in the four corners of the plaint nowhere it is stated that the defendant obtained the decree dated 07-09-77 either by fraud, or by collusion. Thereafter, the Court of appeal below by, referring and relying upon the principles enunciated in the case of Rakhal Chandra vs Benecha Khatun, reported in 24 D.L.R 63 dismissed the appeal.

16. It appears that Court of appeal below in its Judgment nowhere discussed and decided the matter in the light of the provisions of PO 88 and 136 of 1972 read with sections 95 and 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act giving effect that the order passed by the SDO under the provisions of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, which was not challenged under the provision of the same law in the appellate forum or challenged the law in a proper jurisdiction as has been challenged in the case of Hazi Abdul Gani Biswas vs Bangladesh, 26 DLR 394. Moreso, although the trial Court dismissed the suit by referring to the Ruling made in the case of Hazi Abdul Gani Biswas but Court of appeal below failed to notice that before the pronouncement of its judgment the Apex Court by its judgment dated 9-03-1980 reversed the aforesaid judgment of the High Court Division.

17. Considering the materials available on record it appears to this Court that discussing the merit of the case and adverting the reasons given by the Courts below in the judgments would not suffice but it is pertinent to answer some important legal' issues raised by the learned Advocate for the petitioner, which are as follows:—

(a) In view of the decision given by the Appellate Division in Bangladesh vs Haji Abdul Gani Biswas, 32 DLR (AD) 233, whether the judgment and decree passed by the learned Munsif in Title Suit No. 665 of 1976 and affirmed by the Court of appeal below are liable to be set-aside;

(b) whether the order of redemption and possession dated 11-06-1973 passed by the then Sub-Divisional Officer in Miscellaneous Case No. 3579 of 1973 is legal and binding upon the opposite parties.

It appears from the order dated 11-6-1973 passed-by the. Sub-Divisional Officer in Case No. P-3579 of 1973 to the effect that "seen the Ekrarnama" of deed No.6379 dated 17-4-1962 and the opposite party has enjoyed the usufructs of the land for more than 7(seven) years. Hence, ordered that the land is redeemed. The opposite party will hand over the possession of the land to the petitioner forthwith."

18. It further appears that the President's Order No 88 of 1972 came into force on 03-08- 1972, within the stipulated period of agreement, which was scheduled to be due on 12-09-1972 in pursuance of registered deed dated 12-09-62 i.e. within 10 years. So, it is manifested that the case of the petitioner very much falls within the ambit of the PO 88 of 1972, and, as such, order passed by the then Sub-Divisional Officer in Miscellaneous Case will not run from the date of expiry of the agreement but it would be countable, executable and enforceable as per provisions of the PO 88 and 136 of 1972. Since the promulgation of PO 88 of 1972 came into force within the period of stipulation, therefore, the opinion and observation of the Courts below as to the agreement was past and closed was not only misreading of the facts and laws, rather, clear misconception of law, as the order of the then Sub-Divisional Officer was neither beyond the scope of law nor after expiry the period of limitation. The instant suit was filed not for only redemption but also for declaration that the judgment and decree dated 07-09-77 is cancelled as the opposite party obtained the judgment and decree in Suit No. 665 of 1976 touching upon the merit of the case including the question of validity and jurisdiction of PO 88 of 1972. However, the trial Court dismissed the suit in pursuance of the judgment passed by the High Court Division to the case of Hazi Abdul Gani Biswas vs Bangladesh, 26 DLR 394. It is pertinent to mention that while the appeal was pending before the Court of appeal below the Appellate Division by its judgment dated 09-03-1980 reversed the judgment of the High Court Division passed in the case of Hazi Abdul Gani Biswas's mentioned hereinabove and declared that PO 88 and 136 of 1972 are all legal legislation. Therefore, I have no hesitation to opine that the Court of appeal below travelled beyond its jurisdiction in the present case referring to the Ruling made in the case of Rakhal Chandra Das vs Benecha Khatun 24 DLR 63, wherein the principles enunciated is that "after passing the decree it can only be challenged under section 44 of the Evidence Act". But the facts and legal issues related in the present case and legal questions raised by the Bar those are not mere facts but importance question of law touching constitutionality and public importance, which must be decided in the light of the principles enunciated by the Apex Court in the case with similar question of facts and laws.

19. For the reasons stated herein above, it would sufficient to opine that both the Courts below wrongly opined that "the suit filed by the plaintiff petitioner for declaration and specific performance of the contract was hopelessly time barred because the period as stipulated in agreement has already expired long before filing the suit."

20. With regard to the legal issue, (a) as raised by the Bar it will be convenient and relevant to consider section 95 and 95A of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 as amended up to date which runs as follows :-

95. Limitation on mortgage or raiyati holdings—(1) Notwithstanding, anything contained in any other law for the time being in force a raiyat shall not enter into any form of usufructuary mortgage other than a complete usufructuary mortgage in respect of his holding or of a portion or share there, and every such complete usufructuary mortgage shall be subject to the same limitations as are imposed by section 90 on a transfer of the holding of a raiyat or of any share or portion thereof; and the period for which such complete usufructuary mortgage may be entered into by any raiyat shall not exceed, by any agreement express or implied, (seven) years :—

Provided that any such usufructuary mortgage may be redeemed at any time before the expiry of the said period, on payment of an amount which shall bear the same proportion to the total consideration money received by the mortgagor, as the unexpired period bears to the total period for which the mortgage had been entered into.

(2) Every such complete usufructuary mortgage shall be registered under the Registration Act, 1908.

(3) If any usufructuary mortgage entered into by raiyat does not fulfill any of the conditions specified in sub-section (1) or is not registered as required under sub-section (2) it shall be void.

(4) Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, if any mortgagee prevents the redemption of a usufructuary mortgage under the proviso to sub-section (1) or refuses to restore any land covered by a usufructuary mortgage after the expiry of the period of such mortgage, the mortgagor may apply to the Sub-divisional Magistrate or to any officer authorized in this behalf by the Government, for such redemption, or restoration and, on such application and, in the case or redemption, also on payment by the applicant of the amount due to the mortgagee under the said proviso, the Sub-divisional Magistrate or the officer so authorized shall pass an order directing the mortgagee to restore possession of the mortgaged land to the applicant and to deliver up to the applicant all documents in his possession or power relating to the mortgaged land by such date as may be fixed in the order.

(5) If the mortgagee does not restore possession of the mortgaged land to the mortgagor by the date fixed under sub-section (4) the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (or any Officer authorized in this behalf by the Government) shall, on application made by the mortgagor, put the applicant in possession of such land by evicting the mortgagee there from and may, for such eviction, use or cause to be used such force as may be necessary.

Section 95A. Treatment of certain transaction as usufructuary mortgage—Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, any transfer of a holding or of portion or share thereof, (either by way of an out and out sale with an agreement to reconvey,) (or) where the transferor acquires the right to possess, and to enjoy the usufruct of such holding or portion or share thereof for a specified period in lieu of such consideration, shall notwithstanding anything contained in the document relating to the transfer, be deemed to be a complete usufructuary mortgage for a period not exceeding seven years and the provision of section 95 shall apply to such transfer whether made before or after the date of commencement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy (Second Amendment) Order, 1972) ( President's Order No. 88 of 1972)

<u>21. It would not be unworthy to mention here that the legal history of legislation regarding the law of tenancy right and privilege the East Bengal Tenancy Act and the State acquisition and Tenancy Act were amended in the Indian Sub-continent, Erst-while Pakistan and thereafter in Bangladesh for the benefit of the tenants considering the social and economic conditions of the mass people. It is evident from the legal history that for the first time in the year 1929 Section 26G was introduced by amending Act IV of 1928, which came into force on 22-2-1929 the object of the legislature was to protect a raiyat, so that no raiyat can be ousted from possession of his land by a Mohajan wherein he is in possession for more then 15 years. Although in Section 58 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 defined "Mortgage", "mortgagee," "mortgage money" and "mortgage deed" but by amending Act VIII the Bengal Tenancy Act and in Act XXVIII of 1951 introduced a new section namely section 3(3) and 2 (6) respectively. The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act introduced definition of complete usufructuary mortgage", which says complete usufructuary mortgage means of transfer by a tenant of the right of possession in any land for the advanced or to be advanced by way of loan upon the condition that the loan with all interests thereon shall be deemed to be extinguished by the profits arising from the land during the period of Mortgage". Thereby all the raiyat were protected and relieved from all sorts of mortgages except the "complete usufructuary mortgage". Thereafter again sub-sections 4 and 5 in the Section 95 and thereafter 95A were added in the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act,1950 by President's Order No. 88 of 1972, from which it is crystal clear that in the eye of law, no conditional mortgage is valid and any sale with condition of reconvey is a "complete usufructuary mortgage."</u>

<u>22. Once mortgaged, it shall always be deemed to be a mortgage. So, the doctrine of past and closed transactions is not applicable after insertion of the definition of "complete usufructuary mortgage" State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. It further be noted here that in the present case, both the Courts below considered the event of the present case as a sale without considering the exact legal proposition of laws as quoted and discussed hereinabove, for which they came to a wrong decision, and as such, erred in law. The defendant respondent opposite party earlier filed the suit for declaration that the order passed by the then Sub-Divisional Officer is null and void; and with regard to permanent injunction but it transpires from the facts and laws as discussed above that legality and propriety of any order passed by Sub-Division Officer is not amenable under section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, as after the expiry of 7(seven) years the property mortgaged in question deemed to be realized automatically, and as such, the proceeding started by the Sub-Divisional officer not to determine the validity of law or mortgage but it was, in fact for only to pass necessary order. If the mortgagee failed or refused to hand over the possession of the property, if not, handed over in the meantime, and in that case, the Sub-Divisional Officer is authorized to pass order for redemption and also to hand over the possession of the property to the mortgagor.</u>

23. From the discussions and reasons stated herein above, I am of the view that in view of the judgment pronounced by the Apex Court in the Case of Bangladesh vs Haji Abdul Gani, reported in 32 DLR (AD) 233, the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court in TS No. 665 of 1976 affirmed by the appellate Court below is null and void. I am further of the view that PO 88 of 1972 came into force on 03-8-1972 and mortgage in question was valid up to 12-9-1972. Moreover, as per article 148 of the Limitation Act the suit for recovery of the mortgaged property by the mortgagor, the limitation runs for 60 years. Hence, this case is very well covered and attracted by the provisions of PO 88 of 1972, and as such, the judgment passed by the Appellate Division is very much applicable in the present case.

24. Therefore, according to the decisions of the apex Court the judgment and decree dated 07-9-1977 passed in Title Suit No.665 of 1976 has no binding effect upon the plaintiff-petitioner. So, as to the prayer "KW and "Uma" are concerned the plaintiff is entitled to get relief as prayed for.

25. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

26. The judgment and decree dated 14-5-1982 passed by Sub-ordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Khulna in Title Appeal No.172 of 1980 affirming those dated 11-1-1980 passed by the Munsif, 2nd Court, Bagerhat in Title Suit No. 840 of 1977 are hereby set-aside and Title Suit No. 840 of 1977 is hereby decreed, so far as it relates to prayer "kha" and "Uma" for setting-aside the judgment and decree dated 7-09-77 passed by Munsif, 2nd Court, Bagerhat in Title suit No. 665 of 1976 and thereby order dated 11-06-197 passed by Sub-Divisional Officer in Miscellaneous Case No. P-3579 of 1973 is hereby restored.

Send down the lower Court records and communicate this judgment at once.

End.

Vs.
Md. Faizul Huq & Others
full_judgment:
M. A. Khaliq J:- This appeal at the instance of the defendant Nos. 1 and 7 is directed against the judgment and decree passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Sylhet, in Title Appeal No. 182 of 1973 affirming the judgment and decree passed .by the learned Munsif 1st Court, Sadar Sylhet, in Title Suit No. 178 of 1971.

2. Plaintiff filed the suit for declaration of title to recovery of possession in the disputed property he case of the plaintiff is that the disputed property bed to defendant No. 2. During the period' of liberation movement one thatched house standing on the suit land was burnt down. There is another dilapidated tin-shed on the suit premises. Plaintiff filed Money Suit No. 34 of 1970 against defendant No. 2 and obtained decree. In execution of the decree in Money Execution Case No. 49 of 1970 the decree-holder auction purchased the disputed property and took delivery of possession on 10.6.71. On his prayer defendant No. 2 was given 2 (two) months time to remove the but from the suit land Defendant No. 1 is Pir of defendant No. 2 son of Yakub and he used to live in the hut on the suit land till the burning down of the thatched hut. In the vacant portion of the suit land plaint if grew vegetables. Defendant No. 2 did not remove the hut within the period of 2 months as promised and subsequently refused to vacate the land and remove the hut on the asking of the plaintiff. On the other hand he was contemplating to construct some other but in the suit land In such circumstances plaintiff filed the suit.

3. The suit was contested by defendant Nos.1 and 2. According to them one Court Charan Das was the owner of the disputed property. Musai mia and his wife Bidan Bibi took settlement of the disputed property by Kabuliyat dated 3rd Falgoon, 1315 B.S. from Cour Charan Das, Bidan Bibi after the death of Musai got his interest as well. She, therefore, possessed the entire property on his own Yakub was a licensee under Bidan Bibi in respact of the suit premises. Bidan Bibi had no issue. She was survived by brother Adil Mollah who began to possess Bidan's 9 annas share in the property along with other co-sharer. Subsequently by amicable partition Adil Mollah got the suit land. He died leaving daughter Rahima Bibi who was in possession of the property. She transferred the suit land to defendant No. 7 by kabala dated 10th Ashwin, 1377 B.S. Defendant No. 7 while possessing the land constructed house at his own expenses on the suit land. He let out the house to defendant No. 1 at a monthly rent of Taka 25/-. Defendant No. 1 since then has been possessing the disputed property as a tenant under defendant No. 7. It is also the case of the defendants that Ex-Zaminder Court Charan Das transferred his-rent-receiving interest to one Golam Akbar. The disputed property was wrongly recorded in the name of defendant No. 2 and his sister Alpine Defendant No. 2 has got no interest in the suit land. In the above circumstances, the suit is liable to be dismissed. Defendant No. 7 contested the suit on the same ground as that of 'defendant Nos. band 2.

4. The trial Court considered the case on merit and decreed the suit.

5. Being aggrieved defendant preferred Title Appeal No. 182 of 1973. The appeal was heard and disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge, 1st Court Sylhet, The learned Subordinate fudge agreed with the learned Munsif to his finding and decision and as such he dismissed the appeal.

6. Being aggrieved defendant Nos. 1 and 7 preferred this appeal.

7. At the time of hearing of the appeal defendant No. 7 did not proceed with the appeal. So the appeal was taken up at the instance of defendant No. 1. When defendant No. 7 did 'not proceed with the appeal it must be taken that he was ultimately satisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the courts below.

8. Defendant No. 1 the appellant who proceeded with the appeal is admittedly monthly tenant under defendant No. 7 in respect of the disputed property. He cannot, therefore, claim any title to the property except that of his monthly tenancy, When his landlord does not proceed with the appeal it is difficult to understand how he will be benefited by contesting the appeal in the absence of his landlord who is apparently satisfied with the judgment and decree passed by the courts below. As defendant No. 1, the appellant has no claim as to the title of the premises in suit he has no locus standi to proceed with the, appeal.

9. Mr. Ahmed Sobhan, 'the learned Advocate appearing for the defendant No. 1 who is the contesting appellant submits that the lower appellate court based his judgment on mere surmise and conjecture and passed it without considering the patta. Ext. B on the basis of which Bidan Bibi had taken settlement of the dispute property; that the courts below erred in law in holding that Yakub Ali was a tenant in respect of the holding and landlord recognised him as tenant of the disputed property; that the lower appellate court illegally refused.to accept the kabulyat produced at the time of hearing of the appeal, that if Yakub Ali was recognised as tenant by the landlord then how defendant No. 1 possesses the disputed property under defendant No. 7 who purchased it from the heir of Adil Mullah who acquired title to the property of Bidan Bigi after her death; that plaintiff took delivery of possession in the disputed property on 10.6.71 and as such it is void in. view of the provision of P.O. No. 12 of 1972, that the decree obtained by the plaintiff in the Money Suit was fraudulent and collusive, that suit is barred by Article 142 of the Limitation Act, that the suit is bad for defect of parties and in the above circumstances the judgment and decree passed by the Court below are liable to be set aside.

10. Mr. M.A. Hannan, the learned Advocate, appearing for the respondent submits that the decree in the Money Suit was, not exparte decree .and that it was obtained on 10.9.70 and hence the delivery of possession taken by the auction purchaser on 10.6.71 is not hit by P.O. No. 12 of 1972; that the allegations that the decree of Money Suit No. 36 of 1970 was obtained fraudulently and collusively was not raised before the Courts below and there was no' finding and decision on that point and as such it cannot be raised in second appeal; that the courts below gave sufficient reasons why the kabuliyat produced by the defendants before the lower appellate court was not accepted; that the courts below assigned cogent reasons for the finding with regard to the tenancy of Yakub Ali; that the courts below found that Alpina had no heir and as such the question of substitution of her heirs does not arise. According to the learned Advocate the appeal is concluded by finding of facts and as such it is liable to be dismissed.

11. The lower appellate Court has come to the findings that Alpina died without any heir and as such the question of substitution of her heirs does not arise. The objection is; therefore, not tenable in view of the finding of the lower appellate Court.  Ext. B, the patta is in favour of Bidan Bibi but possession has been recorded in the name of Yakub Ali. The case of the plaintiff is that Yakub Ali cook lease of the disputed property from the landlord. The courts below found that Yakub Ali was a tenant in respect of the holding and his tenancy was recognised by the landlord. The courts below held the document Ext. 8 and 9 support the case of the plaintiff, that ex-landlord Gour Charan Das obtained a decree in Money. Suit No. 60 of 1941 against the Yakub Ali for recovery of arrear of rent. The lower appellate Court further held on the basis of Ext. 16 series that ex-landlord Gour Charan Das and his son Prem Chandra Das and subsequent transferee Golam Akbar recognised him as tenant. The learned Advocate for the appellant submits that Ext. 16 series could be manufactured at any time but there is nothing to support the submission of the learned Advocate; on the other hand the courts below found that the documents were very old and they were kept in ordinary course of business and that they are genuine. When the courts below held that Yakut, Ali had tenancy right in the disputed property failure to accept the kabuliyat alleged to have been executed by Bidan Bibi as additional evidence by the lower appellate Court at the appellate stage does not appear to be illegal. It was further held that by the courts below that the property was correctly recorded in the name of Alpine Bibi and defendant No. 2 in Ext. A(1). It was also held that documents Ext. 1-7 produced by the plaintiff prove that he has acquired title to the property and that the plaintiff took symbolical possession in the disputed property on 10.6.71.

12. With regard to the contention that the decree of Money Suit No. 34 of 1970 was obtained fraudulently and collusively it appears that this point was not agitated before the courts below and as such there is no finding and decision on it in such circumstances, the appellant cannot raise that question in second appeal.

13. The plaintiff took delivery of possession in the suit land on 10-6-71 lie filed the suit in 1971 and as such there is limitation.

14. The main contention of the learned Advocate for the appellant is that plaintiff took delivery of possession on 10-6-71 and as such it is hit by P.O. No. 12 of 1972. Ext. 1 certified copy of the order dated 12-8-70 shows that the disputed property was attached before the judgment in Money Suit No. SO of 1970 and subsequently the suit was decreed on compromise. The sale certificate was obtained by the auction purchaser, the plaintiff, on 1.2.71. The decree obtained by the plaintiff was not an ex-parte decree. Defendants appeared in the suit and admitted the claim of the plaintiff` and in his presence the decree was passed. He was, therefore, aware of everything in the suit.

15. The provision of P.O. No. 12 of 1972 is that "all judgments, decrees or orders passed ex-parte by any court or tribunal or orders disposing of matters due to default in compliance with any direction of any court or tribunal in legal proceedings at any time after the 1st day of March, 1971, and before the commencement, of this order (i. e; 7.2.72) are hereby declared mull and void."

<u>16. From the facts stated above it is clear that P.O. No 12 of 1972 does-not apply in the case as the suit was decreed on 18.9.70 and sale certificate was obtained in Execution Case No. 49 of 1970 on 11-2-71. Now the question is whether the delivery of possession taken by the plaintiff on 10-6-71 is hit by P.O. No. 12 of 1972. The delivery of possession given to the plaintiff as auction purchaser on 10-6-71 is neither judgment nor decree nor order passed exparte nor it is an order disposing of any matter due to default in compliance with any direction of any court or tribunal. The decree was obtained in presence of the defendants and with his consent and with his agreement that if he fails to pay up the decreetal dues within a fixed period the decree holder no question of would execute the decree in accordance with law: As he did not pay-up the decreetal dues the decree was executed and the decree holder auction purchased the property and subsequently obtained Sale certificate All these things took place before 1.3.71. The order giving delivery of possession to the plaintiff decree holder auction purchaser was an order consequential to the auction sale and granting of sale certificate to the auction purchaser and, as such not an order contemplated under P.O. No. 12/72. It was also not an original order within the ambit of P.O. No. 12 of 1972.</u>

17. In the above circumstance, I am of the opinion that P.O. No. 12 of 1972 does not affect the delivery of possession in any way. Both the Courts below concurrently found that plaintiffs have tied to the Shit Property and that plaintiff has proved his case and that the defendant could not prove his case as alleged.

18. In the above circumstances, I am of the opinion 'that the appeal is concluded by findings of facts based, on the material on record and it cannot be challenged in second appeal. Secondly the law point raised by the appellant is also not tenable as found above.

19. In the result, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to cost. The connected rule C.R. 1079 (a) 74 which was made absolute and further proceeding of the execution case stayed has become infructuous in view of the judgment.

End.

full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite party No.1 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 allowing the appeal and setting aside the judgment and Order dated 20-4-1998 passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Gazipur in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1996 should not be set-aside.

2. The relevant facts leading to the filing to this revision are as follows :

The opposite Party No. 1, Shakhina as pre-emptor filed Miscellaneous (Pre-emption Case No. 17 of 1996 in the Court of 4th Assistant Judge, Gazipur Sadar, Gazipur seeking pre-emption of the case land under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, 1950 against the Opposite Party No. 1, Abdul Hakim Talukder as pre-emptee purchaser and opposite party No. 2, Monwara Begum as the vendor on the allegation that opposite party No. 2, Monwara Begum sold the case land to opposite party No. 1, Abdul Hakim by a kabala which was executed on 18-6-1996 and with a view to defeat the right of pre-emption the opposite party Nos. 1-2 collusively and cunningly described the deed of transfer as deed of exchange. The pre-emptor and opposite party No. 2, Monwara Begum both are co-sharer of the case holding by inheritance and no notice of transfer was served on her, the opposite party No. 1, Abdul Hakim is a stranger purchaser and hence the pre-emptor is legally entitled to preempt the transfer in question. The opposite party No. 2 as pre-emptee opposite party contested the case by filing a written objection contending that the case is not maintainable in law. The learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Gazipur Sadar after conclusion of trial by its judgment and Order dated 20-4-1994 rejected the said pre-emption case.

3. After passing the said judgment by the trial Court opposite party No. 2 herein transferred 73 decimals land including the case land by a deed of exchange being No. 2042 dated 25-3-1999 to the petitioner.

4. The unsuccessful pre-emptor, thereafter, preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 in the Court District Judge, Gazipur against the judgment and Order passed in Miscellaneous (pre-emption) Case No. 17 of 1996 The said Miscellaneous Appeal was subsequently transferred to the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur for disposal, who by judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 allowed the said appeal upon reversing the judgment and Order passed by the Trial Court.

5. The present petitioner's case in short is that the petitioner having acquired the schedule property by a deed of exchange being No. 2042 dated 25-3-1999, mutated his name and has been enjoying the said land by erecting a two-storied building thereon. The petitioner was not aware about the pre-emption case as well as the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998; that on 29-5-2002 from a notice of Mouchak Police Sub-station, Kaliakoir, the petitioner for the 1st time came to know that the opposite party No. 1 herein as pre-emptor obtained an Pre-emption Order in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 against the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner namely, Md. Abdul Hakim Talukder, herein opposite party No. 2 The said pre-emption Order dated 30-8-2001 passed in the said Miscellaneous Appeal has adversely affected the right, title and interest of the petitioner and hence the petitioner has filed this Revisional Application challenging the Pre-emption Order dated 30-8-2001.

6. The petitioner before filing of this Revisional Application as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 61 of 2003 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur for declaration that the judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 is ineffective and not binding upon the petitioner. The learned Joint District Judge vide its judgment and decree dated 29-1-2007 (decree signed on 5-2-2007) dismissed the said suit on the ground that the petitioner cannot get relief in the suit since he did not challenge the judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 before Higher Court by way of Revision. The learned Judge of the trial Court also found that the suit is not maintainable since the deed of exchange in between the petitioner and opposite party No. 2 was executed during the pendency of the case.

7. The pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 before filing of the original Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Case No. 17 of 1996 as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 before the Assistant Judge, Court No. 4, Gazipur for declaration that the deed of exchange being No. 4346 dated 1-8-1995 (against which Pre-emptor field Pre-emption case) is a sell deed. In the said suit the Pre-emptor (opposite party No. 1 herein) as plaintiff claimed that the impugned deed of exchange was executed only with the view to prevent the right of the pre-emption. After conclusion of the trial learned Assistant Judge, Court No. 4, Gazipur by judgment and decree dated 22-9-1997 (decree signed on 1-10-1997) dismissed the said suit holding that the plaintiff having failed to prove her case that the impugned deed of exchange was a deed of sale.

8. Under the aforesaid facts and circumstance of the case the petitioner has approached before this Court in an application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure and obtained the present Rule.

9. Mr AFM Mesbahuddin, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner at the very outset upon referring to the decisions reported in 49 DLR (AD) 151, PLD 1984 (SC) 166 and 21 DLR (SC) 50 submits that though the petitioner was not party in the original pre-emption case as well as pre-emption miscellaneous appeal but in the facts and circumstance of the case the petitioner has right to protect his right, title and interest by filling Revisional application under section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure since the impugned judgment and Order adversely affected right, title and interest.

10. Mr Mesbahuddin, the learned Advocate on the point of maintainability of the Revisional application submits that the Revisional power of the High Court is a supervisory power which may also be exercised suo moto and any person is competent to bring an illegality into the notice of the High Court and there is no bar of this Court sitting under revisional jurisdiction to rectify the illegality on such information and, as such, in the facts and circumstance of the case this revisional application is well maintainable since the Court of appeal below ignoring a decree passed by a competent Civil Court abruptly arrived at a finding in a summary pre-emption proceeding that the deed in question was out and out sale deed though the learned Assistant Judge on an elaborate discussion of the entire materials on record dismissed Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 by its judgment and decree dated 22-9-1997 (decree signed on 1-10-1997) with the observation that the deed in question was not a deed of sale which was, in fact, an exchange deed.

11. Referring to the judgment and Order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, 4th Court, Gazipur in Pre-emption Misc. Case No. 17 of 1996 the learned Advocate submits that the learned Assistant Judge rightly disallowed the pre-emption case by his judgment and Order dated 20-4-1998 on the findings that the pre-emptor before filing of the Pre-emption Case No. 17 of 1996 filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 before the Assistant Judge, Court No. 4, Gazipur for declaration that the deed of exchange being No. 4346 dated 1-8-1995 (against which Pre-emptor filed the Pre-emption case) is out and out sell deed, not a deed of exchange which was executed as deed of exchange only with the view to prevent the right of the Pre-emption which was dismissed on contest vide judgment and decree dated 22-9-1997 (decree signed on 1-10-1997) and in that view of the matter there is no legal scope to reconsider a decided issue as to the question whether the deed in question was sale or exchange.

12. Mr AFM Mesbahuddin, while elaborating his submission upon placing the judgment and decree dated 22-9-1997 passed in Title Suit No. 63 of 1996, judgment and Order dated 20-4-1998 passed in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1996, judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed in Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Appeal No. 27 of 1998, judgment and decree dated 29-1-2005 passed in Title Suit No. 61 of 2003 and judgment and decree dated 6-6-2005 passed in Title Appeal No. 33 of 2005 by the learned Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur submits that in any event the lower appellate Court acted wrongly and illegally in setting-aside the judgment of the trial Court giving a go by to a unchallenged decree over the self same issue passed by a competent Civil Court in accordance with law and, as such, at any rate the impugned judgment and Order is liable to be set aside.

13. Mr Al Mohammad Ali, the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party No.1, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 which was, according to him just, correct and proper. Mr Mohammad Ali, in the course of his argument after placing the judgments of two Courts below and other relevant materials on record submits that the instant Civil Revision is misconceived and also not maintainable inasmuch as the petitioner was neither a party in appeal not in the original pre-emption case, who as like as a stranger filed this instant Revisional application challenging the impugned judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001.

14. He further submits that this petitioner earlier plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 challenging the impugned judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed by the learned District Judge, Gazipur in Miscellaneous (Pre-emption) Appeal No. 27 of 1998 and thereafter preferred Title Appeal No. 33 of 2005 and after being unsuccessful in both the suit and appeal as 3rd party stranger preferred this Revisional application against the said judgment and Order 30-8-2001 passed by the learned District Judge, Gazipur in Title Appeal No. 27 of 1998. Mr Mohammad Ali, further submits that there is nothing on record to show that the predecessor-in-interest of the present petitioner taken any ground in their written objection or their evidence that the case was barred by law of res-judicata as such the Court of appeal below as last Court of fact committed no illegality in allowing the Pre-emption. 15

15. These are the points which were argued by the learned Advocates for the respective parties. Now, to deal with the contentions raised by the parties before me it would be convenient for me to decide first of all the question of maintainability of the instant Revisional application.

16. The petitioner's case is that petitioner having acquired the case property by way of an exchange deed, mutated his name and has been enjoying the said land by erecting a two-storied building thereon. The petitioner was no aware about the Pre-emption case as well as the Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 2998 who 29-5-2002 for the first time on getting a notice issued by Mouchak Police Sub-station, Kaliakoir came to know that the opposite party No.1 therein as pre-emptor obtained a Pre-emption Order in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 against the predecessor-in-interest of the petitioner namely Md Abdul Hakim Talukder, who is opposite party No. 2 herein. The said Pre-emption Order dated 30-8-2001 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 has adversely affected the rightly, title and interest of the petitioner and as such the petitioner has filed this Revisional Application challenging the Pre-emption Order dated 30-8-2001 though, the petitioner was neither party in the Pre-emption case nor he was made party in the Pre-emption Misc appeal.

17. Now, the cited decisions are required to be referred to for having a better view of the dispute in question as to maintainability of this Revisional Application.

18. In the case of Abdul Qadir vs Abdul Majid reported in 1984 PLD (SC) 166, it has been held that :—

"So far as point No.(i) listed above is concerned, as a general rule no one can appeal or file a revision petition from an Order unless he was a party to the action or was treated as such or was a legal representative of a party or his right in the estate or interest are apparent on the face of the record. For that reason the respondent a pro bono public may not have any interest whatsoever in the cause but that hardly makes any difference. Because we are of the considered view that for the exercise of the revisional powers vested in the High Court, there is no bar for anyone to move the High Court to quash the proceedings which were null and void and the High Court on such move is duty bound to take action in proper cases."

<u>19. In the case of MH Saya & Co. vs Wazir Ali Industries reported in 21 DLR (SC) 50, wherein it has been held that</u>

<u>"There can be no dispute that the only party which was adversely affected by the Order of ad-interim injunction was respondent No. 1. We are satisfied that Saya & Co. deliberately omitted to make them parties with the intention of avoiding a contest. They knew fully well that the relief sought were really directed against Wazir Ali Industries Ltd. and their bankers. A stranger to a suit or a proceeding is not prohibited by the Code of Civil Procedure from filing an appeal from an Order passed therein. It is true that there is no express provision permitting such party to prefer an appeal against such an Order. This omission, however, cannot be understood to amount to prohibition. The Court ought not to act on the principle that every procedure is to be taken a prohibited unless it is expressly provided for."</u>

20. As I have already noticed that impugned judgment and Order of Pre-emption dated 30-8-2001 passed in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 has adversely affected the right, title and interest of the petitioner though, the petitioner was neither party in the original Pre-emption case nor in the pre-emption Misc appeal. Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the case and the principles laid down in the decisions as cited above, I have no hesitation to hold that the instant Revisional application is well maintainable. Besides, no top of that the Revisional power of the High Court Division is supervisory power which may also be exercised suo motu.

21. Now, let me consider whether the Court of appeal below was justified in allowing the Pre-emption after reversing the judgment and Order passed by the learned Assistant Judge in Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1996 on the ground that the deed in question was out and out sale deed.

22. The opposite party No. 1 as pre-emptor filed Pre-emption Misc. Case No. 17 of 1996 for pre-empting the land measuring 59 decimals of land in SA Khatian No. 248/288 under Mouza-Shakashar, PS Kaliakoir, District-Gazipur as described in Deed No. 4336 dated 1-8-1995 on the allegation that the pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 is a co-sharer to the case jote inheritance, after the death of her father her sister, Monwara Begum transferred her share to pre-emptee-opposite party No. 1 beyond the knowledge of the pre-emptor by executing Deed No. 4336 dated 1-8-1995. The opposite party Nos. 1-2 in Order to defeat the right or pre-emption collusively and cunningly described the deed of transfer a deed of exchange. The pre-emptee-opposite party No.1 is a stranger to the case jote and as such the pre-emptor is entitled to pre-empt the land.

23. In the course of trial the learned Assistant Judge upon considering the averments of both the parties framed the following issue:—

(1) Whether the case is in present form?

(2) Whether the case is bad for defect of parties?

(3) Whether the pre-emption application is barred by law?

(4) Whether the deed in question dated 1-8-1995 is a sale deed and the same was registered as deed of exchange in Order to defeat the right of pre-emption?

(5) Whether the pre-emptor is entitled to get the land by way of pre-emption?

(6) Whether the pre-emption is entitled to get any other relives?

24. At the trial both the parties led evidences to prove their respective cases.

25. The trial Court below upon hearing both the sides and on considering the materials on record disallowed the Pre-emption case mainly on 2 (two) counts that: (i) the Pre-emptor-opposite party No. 1 having failed to prove that the deed in question was and out (5) sale deed and (ii) it has been decided earlier in Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 that the deed in question was a deed of exchange, not a sale deed.

26. The Court of appeal below in its turn set-aside the judgment and Order of the trial Court holding that the vendor and vendee in collusion with each other in Order to prevent the right of pre-emption executed a sale deed under the camouflage of a deed of exchange.

27. On a close examination of evidence of PWs and OPWs, I do not find any reliable or corroborative evidence on record to suggest that the pre-emptee-opposite party No. 2, Monwara Begum, sister of the pre-emptor-opposite party sold the case land by executing the kabala in question. Moreover, the opposite party after being unsuccessful to prove that the deed in question was a sale deed in Title Suit No. 63 of 1996 as pre-emptor filed the instant case for pre-emption disputing the self same issue that the deed in question was out and out sale deed without challenging the judgment and decree passed by the learned Assistant Judge in Title Suit No. 63 of 1996. Thus, it appears that so long a valid decree passed by a competent Court on contest against the plaintiff stands the same is binding on him who is present pre-emptor of Pre-emption Miscellaneous Case No. 17 of 1996.

28. The trial Court below on assessment of the entire materials on record by its judgment and Order dated 20-4-1998 disallowed the pre-emption case with the following observations:-

“সর্বোপরি, বাদী নালিশী দলিলকে সাবকবলা দলিল মর্মে ঘোষনার জন্য অত্র আদালতে দেঃ ৬৩/৯৬ নং মোকদ্দমা দায়ের করে। উক্ত মোকদ্দমার কোন কাগজ দাখিল করা না হলেও বাদীনি জেরায় স্বীকার করেন যে, উক্ত মোকদ্দমায় বাদিনী হেরে যান। সাক্ষ্য আইনের ৫৮ নং ধারার বিধান মোতাবেক স্বীকৃত বিষয় প্রমানের আবশ্যকতা নেই। সুতরাং নালিশী দলিলটি সাবকবলা ঘোষনার জন্য বাদী কর্তৃক আনীত মোকদ্দমাটি দো-তরফা শুনানী অন্তে খারিজ হওয়ায় বর্তমান পর্যায়ে একই বিষয় একই পক্ষদের মধ্যে পুনরায় বিবেচনা করার কোন অবকাশ থাকে না যে, উক্ত দলিলটি সাবকবলা দলিল। সুতরাং সার্বিক বিবেচনায় আমি এ সিদ্ধান্ত নিতে সক্ষম হয়েছি যে, নালিশী সম্পত্তি নালিশী দলিল মুলে সাবকবলা বিক্রী হয়নি বরং পক্ষদের সুবিধার্থে এওয়াজ পরিবর্তন করা হয়েছে মাত্র এবং নালিশী দলিলটি একটি এওয়াজ পরিবর্তন দলিল মাত্র।”

29. In the facts and circumstance of the case, I do not find any possible reason to hold that the trial Court below committed any wrong that the deed in question was really a exchange deed, not a sale deed. My view is therefore that the above quoted finding of trial Court is, is fact, based on correct evaluation of the facts and materials of the case.

30. On and overall consideration of the entire materials on record, I am of the view that the Court of appeal below without applying its judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject erroneously held that that the trial Court below committed wrong in rejecting the prayer for pre-emption holding that the pre-emption holding that the pre-emption application is not maintainable as per provision of section 96(1)(B) of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act.

31. Another aspect of the case must not be overlooked.

32. At the fag end of the hearing Mr Minhazul Hoque Chowdhury, the learned Advocate for the petitioner upon referring to mutation of the case land, building plan, rent receipt, electricity bills and some pictures as evidenced by "Annexure-X, Y and Z" series to the supplementary affidavit dated 29-1-2012 submits that the petitioner became owner of the case land by way of exchange deed with opposite party No. 2, A. Hakim Talukder (vendee in pre-emption case) vide deed of exchange being No. 2042 dated 25-3-1999 and the petitioner being owner and possessor of the case land mutated his name vide Mutation Case No. 167/99-2000 in the office of Assistant Commissioner (Land), Kaliakoir, Gazipur and has been paying rent regularly to the Government. He further submits that the petitioner was a government employee and served as Sanitary Inspector and he had no knowledge about the pre-emption proceedings at the time of deed of exchange, who after retirement of his service built a one-storied residential house with five-storied foundation over the case land by spending Taka 21,00,000 approximately. The petitioner has no other residence except the house situated over the case land, if the pre-emption case is allowed the petitioner will be, in fact, homeless.

33. In the facts and circumstances of the case and the materials on record, this last branch of argument of the learned Advocate for the petitioner does not appear to be without any substance.

34. For the reasons stated above, I am inclined to hold that the learned Joint District Judge seriously erred in law in passing the impugned Judgment and Order without properly applying his judicial mind into the facts and circumstances of the case and law bearing on the subject and the same has resulted in an error in the impugned decision occasioning failure of justice.

35. In the result, the Rule is made absolute. The impugned judgment and Order dated 30-8-2001 passed by the learned Judge, 1st Court, Gazipur in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 1998 in set aside.

Let a copy of the judgment along with the lower Court's record be sent down at once.

End.
