full_judgment:
Latifur Rahman, J: This appeal by the defendant-appellant, following leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 4 May, 1994 passed by a single Judge of the High Court Division in Civil Revision No. 1007 of 1992 making the Rule absolute alter setting aside the judgment and order dated 18 February 1992 passed by the Additional District Judge, 4th Court, Comilla in Miscellaneous Appeal No. 66 of 1989 allowing the appeal, after reversing the judgment of the Subordinate Judge, Second Court, Comilla in Misc. Case No. 40 of 1985 under Order IX, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure wherein the Miscellaneous case for setting aside the ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 57 of 1970 (re-numbered as Title Suit No. 9 of 1972) for eviction of defendant-tenant was dismissed.

2. One late Abdus Sattar Khan, predecessor-in-interest of the plaintiff respondents, instituted title Suit No. 57 of 1970 in the 3rd Court of Munsif, Comilla against Sujat Ali Khan, the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant-appellants for eviction from the suit premises on the ground of default and for personal requirements. The plaint case was that the suit property was purchased by him from the original owner by a registered kabala on 29-4-1963 and subsequently the suit property was let out to Sujat Ali Khan at a monthly rental of Tk. 200/- in Baisakh, 1374 B.S. As Sujat Ali Khan was uncle of the plaintiff no bharatia agreement was entered into and the suit was filed as the tenant defaulted in payment of rent and the plaintiff bonafide required the premises.

3. The defendant-tenant contested the suit by filing a written statement denying material allegations of the plaintiff. The defendant late Shujat Ali Khan filed transfer case No. 317 of 1970 in the Court of District Judge, Comilla for transfer of Title Suit No. 57 of 1970 in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge, Comilla for analoguous hearing with his Partition Suit No. 32 of 1970 pending in the Third Court of Subordinate Judge filed against Jaffar khan. Fajar Khan, father of Abdus Sattar Khan for partition of their ejmali properties. The learned District Judge by his order dated 3-5-72 allowed the application and directed simultaneous trial of both the suits namely, suit for eviction and suit for partition, by the third Court of Subordinate Judge, Comilla. On transfer Title Suit No. 57 of 1970, was re numbered as Title suit No. 9 of 1972 and it was decreed ex-parte on 15-8-84 and the partition Suit No. 32 of 1970 filed by Shujat Ali Khan was dismissed for default on 19-3-84.

4. Thereafter on 13-9-85 the Miscellaneous case was filed under Order IX, Rule 13 C.P.C. in the name of late Sujat Ali Khan upon an application filed by his wife Johara Begum contending, inter alia, that both Sujat khan and Jafar khan father of Abdus Sattar acquired the suit property along with other properties by their joint income though purchased in his name for which he already executed a deed of relinquishment and that he has been owning and possessing the suit property on his own right and while contesting the suit was suddenly attacked with paralysis and became bed-ridden for which the opposite party obtained an ex-parte decree practising fraud upon the court and then started Title Execution Case No. 2 of 1985 by suppressing summons. The petitioner could not speak so long but now he could talk but cannot move; that his wife heard of the ex-parte decree when the peon came to give delivery of possession and then upon search in the court on 28-9-1985 became definite and then brought the instant case for restoration.

5. Abdus Sattar Khan, predecessor of the plaintiff-respondents by filing written objection denied the material allegations and asserted that Sujat Ali Khan was neither bed-ridden nor attacked with paralysis and that he did not file any restoration case for dismissal of his Partition Suit No. 32 of 1970.

6. The trial Judge on consideration of the evidence on record dismissed the Miscellaneous case for restoration. The learned Additional District Judge on consideration of the materials on record allowed the appeal after setting aside the judgment and order of the trial Court and restored the suit to its file and number. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division in revision set aside the finding of facts arrived at by the lower appellate Court and restored the judgment of the trial court wherein the Miscellaneous Case under Order IX, Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was dismissed.

7. Leave was granted to consider whether the learned Single Judge of the High Court Division acted wrongly in interfering with the finding of facts of the lower appellate Court in reversing the appellate Courts finding of facts as to illness and incapacity of Sujat Ali Khan which the appellate Court arrived at after close scrutiny of the evidence adduced by the parties.

<u>8. The learned Single Judge of the High Court Division found that it was nowhere stated in the petition that Sujat Ali Khan was attacked with paralysis but in the petition it was only stated that he was suffering from asthma. From the evidence of P.W. 4 Dr. Liaquat Ali it appears that deceased Shujat Khan was bedridden from time to time due to asthma. Further, the doctor deposed that deceased Sujat Ali Khan was taken in his chamber of treatment of asthma. This doctor did not state that Sujat Ali Khan suffered from paralysis nor he deposed that Sujat Khan could not move and speak. He only deposed that he gave prescription for asthma. From the evidence on record the learned Single Judge came to an independent conclusion that the appellant failed to prove that Sujat Ali Khan was suffering from paralysis as a consequence of which he could not take any steps when the suit was taken up for hearing. The learned Single Judge found from the materials on record that the wife of defendant Sujat Khan filed the case for restoration of the suit at a time when defendant Sujat Ali Khan was alive, that Sujat Ali Khan did not give any power to his wife to file the said Miscellaneous case and that Sujat Ali Khan himself did not file the petition. These material aspects were not at all considered by the lower appellate court. The learned Single Judge also found that the original plaintiff Abdus Sattar filed the suit about 25 years back and his successors are not getting the fruits of the decree in the eviction suit. The learned single Judge found that the defendant-petitioner failed to prove by adducing cogent evidence that he was prevented by sufficient cause to appear when the suit was taken up for hearing and disbelieved the story that the defendant was prevented due to paralysis in appearing in the case and consequently dismissed the Miscellaneous case. The learned Single Judge found that non-consideration of the material evidence on record has materially affected the decision of the lower appellate Court occasioning failure of justice. The decision of the lower appellate Court was based on non-consideration of the evidence on record and the appellate Court did not advert to the reasons on which the trial court based its judgment. Hence the learned Single Judge set aside the appellate judgment and restored that of the trial court, rightly it appears.</u>

9. Consequently, the appeal is dismissed without any order as to costs.

End.

case_source: Arising out of the judgment and decree passed by Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet, in Title Appeal No.121 of 1989 affirming those dated 7.3.89 passed by learned Subordinate, Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet, in. T.S. No.303 of 1984
full_judgment:
Syed Fazle Ahmed, J.: These two rules call in question the legality and propriety of the judgment and decree passed by Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet, in Title Appeal No.121 of 1989, affirming those dated 7.3.89 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet, in T.S.No.303 of 1984.

2. Opposite party Nos. 1-4 as plaintiffs instituted T.S. No.2 of 1964 before the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet, for partition of the suit land claiming 1/3rd share therein and subsequently it was renumbered as T.S.No.14 of 1966.

3. Defendant No. 1 had filed written statement stating inter alia that he had taken jote settlement of about 1½  Hals of land out of the suit land from its original owners and since then he had been in exclusive possession therein on payment of rent to the ex-landlord; that during survey operation the land was duly recorded in the name of the defendant and that plaintiffs and other defendants have no right, title, interest and possession in the said land and as such the suit is liable to be dismissed. Other defendants also entered appearance by filing written statement and put forward their respective claims in the suit land.

4. The suit was taken up for hearing by the learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Additional Court, Sylhet, and on conclusion of the trial the suit was decreed in preliminary from by the judgment and decree dated 21.2.66. Thereafter, Advocate commissioner was appointed to effect "partition of the suit land in terms of the preliminary decree and that in the meantime defendant No.1 (ga) and 1 (gha) prayed for separate saham in the suit land by filing petition dated 22.4.86 and 26.4.86 respectively and the learned Subordinate Judge allotted separate saham to the said defendants by his order dated 30.7.87. The learned Advocate commissioner conducted the survey in his own way and erroneously relayed the suit land covering about half beyond the suit land and leaving aside eastern side of the suit land and thereafter submitted perfumery report dated 9.7.88 to the learned Subordinate Judge.

5. Thereafter, the petitioners filed written objection against the report on 17.11.88 being supported by an affidavit stating that the learned advocate commissioner exceeded his jurisdiction and acted beyond the scope of warrant of commission; that he left a portion of  the suit lend on its east and included wrongly left portion or the west of the suit land and encroached the lend of the petitioners which is not covered by the suit land.

6. Thus, the report of the advocate commissioner is perverse and not sustainable under the facts and circumstances of the case. Certified copy of the objection filed by the petitioners against the report of the advocate commissioner is annexed and marked as annexure 'A' to the petition. Other defendants also filed written statement, raised objection against report of the learned advocate commissioner on various specific grounds.

7. In the meantime defendant No.1(kha) Bela Bibi @ Pesi Bibi made an application dated 7.12.88 with a prayer for allotting saham to her. Thereafter, upon prayer mad by the petitioners, the learned Subordinate Judge was pleased to issue summons upon the Advocate Commissioner to appear as witness before the Court. Thereafter on two occasions the suit was adjourned fixing 26.2.89 for hearing of the objection as well as other application, made by defendants. Thereafter on 26.2.89 the learned Advocate Commissioner appeared before the Court as witness but the Court being engaged otherwise, the matter was fixed on 7.2.89. Subsequently Advocate Commissioner being indisposed could not attend court and the objection filed against the Commissioner's report could not be take up for hearing by the learned Subordinate Judge. Subsequently it was on 9.3.89 that the learned Subordinate Judge rejected the objection filed against report of the Advocate Commissioner without affording opportunity to the parties of being heard and that the learned Subordinate Judge accepted the report filed by the learned Advocate Commissioner upon making the preliminary decree final by his judgment and decree dated 7.3.89. Thereafter petitioner made another application before the learned Subordinate Judge on 11.3.89 for vacating the order dated 7.3.89 suing reasons, but the same was not entertained by the learned Subordinate Judge and it was rejected by his order dated 11.3.89.

8. Thereafter petitioner as appellant preferred Title Appeal No. 121 of 1989 before the learned District Judge, Sylhet, as against the aforesaid judgment and decree dated 7.3.90. Defendant No.1 (kha) preferred cross-objection No. 5 of 1989 as against the selfsame judgment and decree while defendant No.4 Md. Jafi preferred Title Appeal No. 106 of 1989 as against the same decree.

9. The aforesaid two appeals namely T.A. No. 121 of 1989 and T.A. No. 106 of 1989 and the cross-objection No.5 of 1989 were taken up for hearing analogously by the Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet, who by his judgment and decree dated 20.8.90 dismissed both the appeals and cross-objection.

10. Being aggrieved by the aforesaid judgment, petitioner moved the revisional jurisdiction of this Court and obtained the present Rules which have been numbered as Civil Revision Nos.2066 and 2067 of 1990 and both the aforesaid Civil Rules cropped up out of the same judgment and decree referred above.

11. The learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in both the Rules submitted that the report prepared by the Advocate Commissioner was not in accordance with the terms embodied in the preliminary decree and he prepared that report whimsically and arbitrarily ignoring the terms of the preliminary decree and as such the report was totally perverse affecting the interest of the parties prejudicially. An opportunity was provided by the learned Subordinate Judge to file objection against the report submitted by the Advocate Commissioner and accordingly petitioner availing that opportunity filed objection against the report of the Advocate Commissioner on 17.11.88 vide Annexure `A' to the petition. It is further urged that the learned Advocate Commissioner appeared before the Court on 26.2.89 upon filing hajira but the court being engaged otherwise could not take up the matter and adjourned it to 7.3.89. It is further urged that the provision laid down in Order 26, sub-rule 2 of Rule 14 C.P.C. ejoins that court after hearing any objection which the parties may make to the report, "shall confirm" vary or set aside the same and this provision expressly provides that sufficient opportunity must be given to the parties to file objection to the report and that such objection is to be adjudicated upon by the Court on merit and thereafter final decree is to be drawn. The learned Advocate continued to urge that High Court has power to see whether Commissioner has exceeded his jurisdiction or acted within the scope of his warrant of the commission. In this connection the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner has relied on the decision in the case of Nazir Ahmed and another Vs. Surfazur Rahman and others, reported in A.I.R 1935 (Lahore) page 501 and urged that the Commissioner should be examined first and if there is ground for further enquiry, party should be allowed to produce evidence. It is further urged that Court, after hearing any objection which the party may make shall confirm, vary or aside the same and thus it is implied that parties are entitled to substantiate their objection on adducting evidence. But in the instant case opportunity was not afforded to the parties to examine the advocate commissioner nor any opportunity was afforded to lead evidence in support of the objection and that the court arbitrarily accented the report without giving opportunity of being heard. The learned advocate continued to urge that objection against the advocate commissioner's report was filed on 17.11.88. and in between the date of filing objection and till the date of hearing of the objection on 7.3.89 on seven occasions this matter was adjourned and out of seven occasions, on 3 occasions i.e. 28.1.88, 10.1.89 and 26.2.89 Court was engaged otherwise and on 8.2.89 summon was issued to the Advocate Commissioner asking him to attend Court on 26.2.89 and the Commissioner attended the Court on that date by filling hajira; that the Court being engaged otherwise the matter was adjourned on 7.3.89 and that without disposing of the objection filed against the Commissioner's report, final decree was drawn up arbitrarily. Against the back ground of this facts it is submitted that the learned Subordinate Judge committed error of law in not complying with the mandatory provision laid down in Order 26, sub-rule 2 of Rule 14 C.P.C. and error in law having been committed erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice has occurred.

12. In reply to this contention the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties in both the Rules urged that petitioners are not entitled to any relief in as much as no error in law resulting in erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice has occurred in this case. It is further urged that Order No.14 dated 7.3.89 shows that objection filed against the Advocate Commissioner's report was heard and it was rejected and as such the submission made by the learned Advocate that objection filed against Advocate Commissioner's report remained undisposed of, does not stand to reason. So far cross-objection filed by Bala Bibi, it is urged application made by Bala Bibi seeking allotment of saham was rejected by the Court and this order of rejection being not appealable as per provision contained in Order 41 Rule 22 sub-rule 1 C.P.C. Bala Bibi has no locus standi to prefer cross-objection. In support of this contention the learned Advocate relied on the decision reported in A.I.R 1964 (Patna) page 298 and A.I.R. 1934 (Allahabad) page 543.

13. The learned Advocate representing Bala Bibi submits that order by which any injustice has occasioned, the revisional jurisdiction can be invoked to correct such injustice and in support of this contention the decision in the case of Gunendralal Das Chowdhury and ors. Vs. Nitandralal Das Chowdhury, reported in 21 DLT (1969) page 361 has been relied upon.

14. I have been taken through the impugned judgment and decree passed by Additional District Judge, Sylhet, in T.A. No. 106 and 102 of 1989 and cross-objection No. 5 of 1989.

15. It has already been pointed out earlier that after passing of the preliminary decree in T.S. No.14 of 1966 by the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet, Advocate Commissioner was appointed to effect partition as per terms embodied in the preliminary decree and thereafter Advocate Commissioner having completed the survey, submitted report and parties were given opportunity to file objection against the report of the Advocate Commissioner. Objection was filed against the report of Advocate Commissioner on 17.11.88 vide Annexure 'A' to the petition.

16. Now it is to be considered if objection was disposed of by the learned Subordinate Judge on merit. It is submitted on behalf of the opposite party that the objection filed against the Advocate Commissioner's report was heard and disposed of and thereafter final decree was drawn up on the basis of the preliminary decree passed in T.S. No. 14 of 1966 on 21.2.66. The order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge reads thus:-

১৪৫/(১৮-২-৮৯)

প্রার্থীত মতে বিবাদী পক্ষের আনিত স্বাক্ষীর প্রতি পক্ষের নিজ দায়িত্বে সমন জারী হউক।

স্বাঃ আব্দুল মকিত মজুমদার 	এস,জি-২

১৪৬/(১৬-২-৮৯)

স্বাক্ষীগণ হাজিরা দিয়েছেন। ৪নং বিবাদী নিষেধাজ্ঞার বিরুদ্ধে এফিডেভিট সহকারে আপত্তি দাখিল করিয়াছেন। কপি দেওয়া হইয়াছে। তাহা নথিতে রাখা হউক। বিচারক স্বত্ব ১১৮/৮৬ নং মামলাতর বিচার কার্য্যে ব্যস্ত থাকায় আগামী ৭-৩-৮৯ ইং তারিখ আপত্তি শুনানী দং শুনানী ও নিষেধাজ্ঞা শুনানীর জন্য রাখা গেল।

স্বাঃ আব্দুল মজিত মজুমদার

এস,জি-২

১৪৭/(৭-৩-৮৯)

পক্ষগণ হাজিরা দিয়াছেন। মামলা দরখাস্ত শুনানী, আপত্তি শুনানী ও নিষেধাজ্ঞা ও শুনানীর জন্য পেশ করা গেল। পক্ষগণের বিজ্ঞ কৌশলীগণের বক্তব্য শুনলাম। নথীপত্র পর্যালোচনা করিয়া দেখিলাম। প্রাথমিক ডিক্রীতে ১(খ) নং বিবাদীর কোন স্বত্বাংশ নিরাকরণ করা হয় নাই। বিধায় অত্র দরখাস্ত রক্ষণীয় নহে বলিয়া অগ্রাহ্য করা গেল। কমিশনারকে আপত্তিকারী পক্ষ নিজ দায়িত্বে স্বাক্ষী মানা সত্বেও হাজির করেন নাই বা হাজির করিবার জন্য কোন পদক্ষেপ নেন নাই বিধায় কমিশনার দাখিলী রিপোর্টের বিরুদ্ধে আপত্তি অগ্রাহ্য করা গেল। এতদমর্মে কমিশনারের দাখিলী রিপোর্ট গ্রহণ করা হইল। মামলা চুড়ান্ত নিস্পত্তির জন্য লওয়া হইল। অতএব আদেশ হইল যে, বিগত ২১/২/৬৬ ইং তারেখের প্রাথমিক ডিক্রী চুড়ান্ত করা হইল। কমিশনারের রিপোর্ট, ম্যাপ, চিটা, শিডবুক ইত্যাদি চুড়ান্ত ডিক্রীর একাংশ হিসাবে গণ্য করা হউক।

17. The order quoted above shows that entire blame has been thrown on the petitioner for not procuring attendance of the Advocate Commissioner on the date of hearing. But it has already been pointed out that on 18.2.89 summons was issued to the Advocate Commissioner directing him to attend Court on 26.2.89 and on that date Commissioner attended the Court by filing hajira. This fact is borne out by the entire order-sheet placed before this Court. The court being engaged otherwise could not take up the hearing of the matter and so it was adjourned to 7.3.89. Thus the observation made by the learned Subordinate Judge that no step was taken by petitioner to procure attendance of Advocate Commissioner in Court is wholly unwarranted and against the weight of evidence on record. The learned Subordinate Judge without affording any opportunity to the parties concerned arbitrarily accepted the report without disposing of the objection on merit and drew up the final decree on 21.2.66 on the basis of the preliminary decree passed in T.A. No.14 of 1966. Legal provision referred above expressly provides that sufficient opportunity must be given to the party to file objection against the report of the Advocate Commissioner before the final decree is drawn up. Introduction of the word "vary" in sub-rule 2 of Order 26 Rule 14 of the C.P.C. enables the Court to modify the report in proper case and the Court's view on the subject should be treated to be final.

<u>18. The order recorded by the learned Subordinate Judge, by no stretch of imagination, it can be held that the objection filed against Advocate Commissioner's report was adjudicated upon by the Court concerned. Although there is no provision in the C.P.C. entitling a party who objects to the report of the Advocate Commissioner to produce evidence in support of his objection. But the provision contained in Order 26 Rule 14 Sub-rule 2 C.P.C. provides that the Court after hearing any objection which the party may make to the report shall "confirm, vary or set aside" the same. This implies that the parties are entitled to substantiate their objection but in such cases, as rule of practice, the Advocate Commissioner should first be examined with reference to the objection and if it appears from the statement of the Advocate Commissioner that there is a ground for further enquiry into the matter which is in the objection, then the parties should be allowed to produce evidence or the Advocate Commissioner be directed to amend his report accordingly.</u>

19. Thus is appears that the mandatory provision of law has been totally ignored by the learned Subordinate Judge in not disposing of the objection filed against the Advocate Commissioner's report on merit and he has, by his impugned order, denied the right to the parties concerned of being heard and to lead evidence in support of objection raised against the report. It has already been pointed out that adequate step was taken by the petitioner to summon the Advocate Commissioner on the date fixed by the Court and the Advocate Commissioner, in fact, attended Court by filing hajira, but the Court being engaged otherwise the matter was adjourned to 17.11.88. But on that date further opportunity was not afforded to the parties, rather the Court arbitrarily by the impugned order accepted the report without impugned order accepted the report without disposing of the objections on merit raised against the Advocate Commissioner's report and thereby the Court committed error in the law which resulted in erroneous decision occasioning failure of justice.

20. The interest of justice will be served, if this matter be heard again by the learned Subordinate Judge 2nd Court, Sylhet, So to secure ends of justice and to enable the petitioner to lad evidence in support of objection filed against report of Advocate Commissioner, the matter need to be remanded to Court concerned for disposing if the objection filed against the Advocate Commissioner's report on merit.

21. Now, I pass over to cross-objection filed by Bala Bibi. The learned Subordinate Judge observed in his impugned order that Bela Babi who figured as defendant No.1 (kha) was not allotted any saham in the preliminary decree and as such application seeking allotment of share was turned down. In this connection the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite party submits that since application of Bala Bibi was rejected and that order of rejection being not appealable under the provision of Order 41 sub-rule 1 of Rule 22 C.P.C. she has no locus standi to prefer objection inasmuch she has no right to appeal.

22. It appears that Bala Bibi's sisters respondent No.39 and 41 who figured as respondent No.1 (ga) and 1(gha) were allotted saham and therefore there is no reason why Bala Bibi who happens to be full sister of respondent 39-41 should be deprived of the saham claimed by her.

23. It is true that Bala Bibi's saham was turned down by the learned Subordinate Judge on the ground that she was not allotted any share in the preliminary decree.

24. Now it is to be seen if High Court exercising revisional jurisdiction can correct the injustice done to Bala Bibi In this connection it has already been referred that two sisters of Bala Bibi respondents 39 to 40 were allotted sham on the basis of application preferred by those two sisters and so there is no earthly reason why Bala Bibi should be deprived of her share which she is legally entitled to the High Court when seized of the revision proceeding as a whole is competent to look into the matter from start to finish because the object of scutising of the proceeding as a whole by the High Court, is that justice may be done as a whole in the proceeding. In this connection the the decision in the case of Rati Ram Vs. Naiser Mal, reported in A.I.R. 1941 (Allahbad) page 215, has been relied upon. His Lordshipe observed as follows:

"Once the High Court is seized of the revision, then it becomes its duty to cast its eye not merely on one part of the proceedings but the whole of them. What came under the review of the High Court are the proceedings as a whole from start to finish and the object of the scrutiny of the High Court is that so far as possible justice may be done in the proceedings as a whole."

25. The learned Advocate also relied on another decision in the case of Gunendralal Das Chowdhury & ors -Vs.- Nitandralal Das Chowdhury, reported in 21. DLR. page 361. His Lordship has observed as follows:

“Provision under Section 115 C.P.C. is wide enough to call for an interference, particularly because the High Court can suo motu interfere with a wrong decision under this section."

26. It has already been found that when Bala Bibi's sisters had been allotted share, there is no reason why Bala Bibi should be denied the privilege of being allotted saham. Order 41 Rule 22 sub-rule 1 C.P.C. does not stand on the way in removing the injustice done to Bala Bibi by the impugned order passed by the learned Subordinate Judge.

27. Thus, having considered the entire materials on record, facts and circumstances and legal aspect of the matter, the impugned order passed by the learned Additional District Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet, in Title Appeal No.106 of 1989 and T.A. No. 121 of 1989 are hereby remitted to the Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court. Sylhet, for disposal of the objection after affording chance to the petitioners to lead evidence in support of the objection raised and thereafter to dispose of the objection on merit within six months from the date of receipt of the record from this Court. Parties are directed to bear their respective cost.

28. Cross-objection filed by Bala Bibi Also remitted to learned Subordinate Judge, 2nd Court, Sylhet for disposal on merit.

29. In the result, both the rules are thus made absolute as indicated above.

End.
